label: Ragusano

names.text: "Asino Ragusano" taken from the Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch (its interlanguage and source names give Asino Ragusano and Âne ragusano). "Ragusana" is from the intake list and appeared in WebSearch result text describing a study of 'Martina Franca and Ragusana asses'; the Wikipedia article does not give it, and the page behind that search text could not be opened, so "Ragusana" is unconfirmed.

about.text: An Italian donkey breed from Sicily, associated with the comuni of Modica, Ragusa, Santa Croce Camerina and Scicli in the province of Ragusa. It is especially valued for siring mules and for producing asses' milk, and is also used for transport, agricultural work and trekking.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the comuni, the uses (transport, agricultural work, trekking) and the mule siring and asses' milk statement.

origin.place: The province of Ragusa in southern Sicily. Developed at the Istituto di Incremento Ippico in Catania, from the Grigio Siciliano and Pantesco donkeys, with some influence from the Asino di Martina Franca and the Catalan donkey; official breed recognition in 1953.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: the province, the development at the Catania institute, the ancestor breeds, and recognition in 1953. The article gives only that the earliest mentions date to the mid-19th century, so no formation years are given.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "2007 (FAO): 349 animals."
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch, citing DAD-IS: 5,013 head in 723 herds, including 3,537 registered breeding jennies and 450 breeding jacks. Taken from the article, not from DAD-IS itself.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: uses listed as transport, agricultural work and trekking; the breed is especially valued for siring mules and for producing asses' milk. The order is a judgement: the article names mule siring and asses' milk as the breed's chief values, so dairy is listed first.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: DAD-IS 2025 "vulnerable"; and FAO 2007 "endangered". DAD-IS itself could not be opened, so the 2025 status is as the article reports it.

facts.v: Wikipedia says donkey milk has antiviral properties and could help prevent viral gastrointestinal infections, citing Brumini et al. (2013) on echovirus type 5. That study is on donkey milk protein fractions, not on Ragusano milk specifically.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "has been found to have anti-viral properties" and the Brumini et al. (2013) citation in International Dairy Journal. The cited study itself was not opened.

gaps: No milk composition or yield figures found for the Ragusano; DAD-IS was not opened directly (its 2025 status and 2023 count are as Wikipedia reports them); the earliest mentions are only given as mid-19th century, so no formation years; the Brumini et al. (2013) study was not opened.
